mechanism_narrative: The four-week monotonic decline in WORKPLACES (-13.9 to -56.3) and TRANSIT (-41.3 to -73.6) reflects deepening suppression of out-of-home activity that directly removes foot traffic available to retail and recreation venues, so RETAIL_REC will continue its downward trajectory over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both series show consecutive weekly declines over last 4 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the last-28-day mean even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue to decline week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility crossing above +20 points indicates near-saturation of stay-at-home compliance under the national state-of-alarm lockdown; once this threshold is breached, further compliance tightening suppresses discretionary retail trips for the subsequent two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL reached 21.3 at t-1w and 24.3 at t-0w, crossing the +20 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises in the two weeks following a RESIDENTIAL reading above +20, despite the threshold being met.

mechanism_narrative: The parallel decline of GROCERY_PHARM (8.0 to -22.1) alongside RETAIL_REC indicates households are reducing even essential shopping frequency through bulk-buying and delivery substitution, a behavioral adaptation that will keep RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from +8.0 to -22.1 over the four observed weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM continues to decline, breaking the co-movement assumption.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week PARKS increase greater than 8 points (as observed from t-1w to t-0w, -53.1 to -42.6) reflects a seasonal spring pull toward outdoor recreation once any mobility slack is permitted, which would partially spill over into increased retail-adjacent outdoor trips within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 8 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -53.1 at t-1w to -42.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline over the next two weeks despite PARKS rising more than 8 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous deep declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES create a reinforcing feedback: reduced transit use curtails access to workplaces, and reduced workplace attendance further lowers transit demand, jointly compounding the suppression of retail footfall beyond what either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both declined every week over the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decline over the next four weeks is no steeper than predicted by either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES alone, indicating no interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week RESIDENTIAL increase exceeding 2 points signals intensifying home-centric consumption habits (online ordering, reduced errands) that substitute for in-person retail visits, producing a further decline in RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises more than 2 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 21.3 to 24.3 (3.0 points) between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week following a RESIDENTIAL rise greater than 2 points, contradicting the substitution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: Under the continuation of Spain's national state of alarm with no announced relaxation, all mobility categories tied to discretionary movement (RETAIL_REC, WORKPLACES, TRANSIT) will remain near their current troughs or decline marginally further, since the regulatory floor has not been lifted as of the decision date.
evidence_refs: fact:all three series show sustained large negative percent changes through t-0w with no reversal
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days rises meaningfully above the last-28-day mean despite no observable policy relaxation signal in the snapshot.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT readings stabilize within a 5-point band across two consecutive weeks (unlike the sharp drops seen from t-3w to t-0w), this signals that mobility suppression has reached a floor, after which RETAIL_REC should also stabilize or mildly recover within two weeks as the marginal deterrent effect saturates.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week change stays within a 5-point band for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell by 23.8, 5.3, and 3.2 points in successive weeks, showing decelerating decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline over the next two weeks even after TRANSIT stabilizes within a 5-point band for two consecutive weeks.
